title: Deployment Reproducibility Evidence Bundle v1
description: Raw, committed measurement evidence backing a reproducibility manifest (see reproducibility.schema.json's evidenceFile). Contains ONLY captured facts — live on-chain runtime bytecode (read via a public RPC at one resolved block, never a moving 'latest' label) and two independently-captured compiler builds (pinned to the historical deployment commit, and to current public HEAD), each with solc's own deployedBytecode.object and immutableReferences verbatim, plus sourceDigests (per local source file keccak256, captured on disk at capture time) and immutableAstDeclarations (every `immutable` VariableDeclaration the compiler's own AST reported — a machine-derived authority, independent of immutableIdentities' hand-typed labels). This file does NOT contain any derived verdict (no match/hash/verified booleans) — those are computed deterministically and offline from this evidence by scripts/lib/reproducibility-evidence.ts every time `npm run validate:reproducibility` runs, so they can never drift from what this file actually contains. When the validator has repo access, it additionally re-verifies deploymentCommitBuild.commit/publicHeadBuild.headCommit and their sourceDigests against the ACTUAL git objects at those commits (requires a full-history checkout) — see verifySourceDigestsAgainstCommit and verifyReportedCommitInPublicHistory.

subject.description: The deployed contract name (matches the corresponding manifest's subject).

liveRuntime.description: A genuine external measurement: the live on-chain runtime bytecode, captured via a public RPC read at ONE resolved block (eth_blockNumber, resolved once, then reused for both eth_getBlockByNumber and eth_getCode — never a moving 'latest' label re-resolved between calls). Not independently authenticated against Ethereum consensus (no state/account proof); trusted as recorded, with runtimeCodeHash provable as self-consistent (keccak256(runtimeBytecode)) by the checker.

blockNumber.description: The exact block number resolved once at capture time.

capturedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the RPC read.

runtimeCodeHash.description: keccak256(runtimeBytecode), computed by the capture tool independently of the RPC response's own framing; the checker recomputes and cross-checks this.

deploymentCommitBuild.description: Compiled from a worktree pinned to the exact historical deployment commit, using that commit's own committed lockfile/toolchain.

publicHeadBuild.description: Compiled from current public HEAD at capture time, using the repo's current lockfile/toolchain — a distinct capture from deploymentCommitBuild, since the toolchain can (and here, did) drift between the two commits.

immutableIdentities.description: Only present for contracts with `immutable` variables. One entry per compiler-reported immutable AST id (not per physical byte-range reference — a single immutable can be referenced at multiple PUSH sites; see deploymentCommitBuild.immutableReferences for the physical offsets).

astId.description: The solc AST node id of the VariableDeclaration, as a string (matches a key in immutableReferences).

derivation.description: The exact public-input computation the checker re-runs to derive this immutable's expected 32-byte value. See scripts/lib/reproducibility-evidence.ts deriveImmutableExpectedBytes for the implementation of every method.

expectedValueHex.description: Pinned expected value, for auditability. The checker independently recomputes this from `derivation` and fails if it disagrees with what's pinned here, so this can never silently drift from the derivation it claims to record.

deployedBytecodeObject.description: solc's own evm.deployedBytecode.object, verbatim, 0x-prefixed. Zero-filled at any immutable byte ranges (solc's own convention for the pre-patch template).

immutableReferences.description: solc's own evm.deployedBytecode.immutableReferences, verbatim, keyed by AST node id (as a string). Empty object for a contract with no `immutable` variables.

sourceDigests.description: keccak256 of the LITERAL content embedded in the compiler's OWN standard-json input for every compiled LOCAL project source file (paths under contracts/, tracked in this repo's git history) — NOT a disk snapshot taken separately. Proven by construction to be exactly what produced deployedBytecodeObject; re-verified by the checker against the claimed commit's actual git objects (git show) whenever it has repo access. Third-party dependency sources (e.g. node_modules-resolved @openzeppelin/... imports) are deliberately excluded here: they aren't tracked in this repo's git history, so a git-commit binding check can't apply to them — package-lock.json's own integrity hashes (enforced by `npm ci`) already cover that; they ARE still folded into compilerInputHash below.

compilerInputHash.description: keccak256 of a canonical (recursively key-sorted) JSON serialization of the FULL solc standard-json input (language, ALL sources including dependencies, settings) that produced this build — a single audit fingerprint of the complete compilation input, freezing even the parts (dependency source content) git does not govern. For a Hardhat-3 split input/output pair, the pairing is proven via the tool's own matching `id` field on both files, not merely a filename convention.

immutableAstDeclarations.description: Every VariableDeclaration the compiler's OWN AST reports with mutability "immutable", across the whole compilation unit for this build — captured mechanically by the capture tool, independent of any hand-typed immutableIdentities label. The checker requires every AST id physically referenced in immutableReferences to appear here; an id that does not is refused authority to claim any exclusion range, however plausible-looking its accompanying (hand-typed) immutableIdentities entry is.
